title: DR1 calls the second consignment role "Consignor"; the frontend calls it "Consignor or exporter".

finding.frontend: The role is named "Consignor or exporter" on the consignment addresses page and again as the heading of the page that picks it, from one copy entry (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:20-24). It is the only one of the five roles whose name differs from DR1's; the hint under it, "This is the sender of the consignment.", is word for word the same on both sides.
finding.prototype: DR1 names it "Consignor" in both places, and the link that opens it reads "Add a consignor" (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:15-27). The URL behind it is /consignor-or-exporter and DR1 accepts addresses typed consignor or exporter for it, so the role covers the same ground — it is only the name shown to the user that is shorter.
finding.difference: Rename the role to Consignor wherever the trader sees it: the consignment addresses row, the picker heading and the visually hidden text on the row's action. The frontend keeps one copy entry for all three, so this is one string. The identifier and the URL slug are not part of the change.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding "exporter" in any heading, link or row label DR1 shows the user for this role.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs for fe-addresses-hub, fe-address-picker-consignor-or-exporter, dr1-roles-and-addresses and dr1-consignment-address-select, the fe-addresses-hub and dr1-roles-and-addresses-partial screenshots, and both copy sources at the cited lines; ran the falsifier by grepping every heading, link and section label DR1 renders for this role. It does not fire — DR1 shows "Consignor" and "Add a consignor" and never the word exporter, while the alias list at app/routes.js:3443 keeps exporter as a stored type only. Checked the "only one of the five" claim against all five role names on both sides: Place of origin, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination match word for word, and the consignor hint matches too. CORRECT.
